feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iterations 0 to 3 gave identical metrics to four decimals on all tracks (score 26.0449, one line-loss event per trial, max_error 0.0609 to 0.0614 m, progress 0.035 to 0.115). Those iterations changed spread (iteration 1), footprint (iteration 2) and wheel_track (iteration 3), so none of those geometry axes has moved the score. The off-track floor of 0.06 m binds, because body_width cannot lift it. Your wheel_radius 0.04 m test is a sensible single-variable probe. A larger radius raises ground speed per PWM and the wheel-speed difference per turn command, so yaw response should rise, and progress and completion_time should move first. Next-race rules: (a) if the metrics again match iterations 0 to 3 to four decimals, stop geometry changes and treat the pipeline as the blocker; (b) if progress or completion_time changes but line_loss_events stay at one or more with max_error near 0.06 m, the robot is still losing the line, so the next lever is controller gain, not geometry; (c) if max_error falls below 0.06 m and line_loss_events reach zero, keep wheel_radius 0.04 m and vary one other geometry value.
requested_changes: Keep wheel_radius at 0.04 m with all other values from iteration 3 for one race. If the metrics match iterations 0 to 3 exactly, stop geometry changes and check the race data pipeline.
If the metrics change but line_loss_events stay at one or more, hold the geometry and test a controller gain change (kp 2.0 to 3.0) to see whether the limit is steering response rather than geometry.
If progress rises but steering_oscillation becomes high, test wheel_radius 0.035 m as the midpoint to back off the speed and yaw response while keeping the sensor geometry fixed.
